reasons.C1: Latent channels beating text monitors matter, but non-adaptive channels make the snapping defeat expected; no colluding agents, channels mostly trained pre-sprint.
reasons.C2: Strong controls: swapped, zero, no-message at 0.000, shuffled-label probe control, 10 of 10 checkpoints reproduced, text baseline; few seeds, no significance tests.
reasons.C3: Figure 1 makes the core claim instantly; 13 pages likely exceed the 8-page cap and the collusion link is underexplained.

levers.C1: Train channels adversarially against snapping and probes, and embed them in a collusion game where two agents gain from hidden coordination.
levers.C2: Add an adaptive-channel arm with five or more seeds and significance tests, and publish checkpoints so others can rerun everything.
levers.C3: Cut to 8 pages with one framing paragraph tying carrier results to agent collusion and a single results table.

Q4.verdict: Clean, well-controlled carrier study with convincing negative controls, but it measures a channel, not collusion, against an easy non-adaptive opponent.

reasons.C1: Testing fines, leniency and rewards on LLM cartels against a published human benchmark is policy-relevant and goes beyond the usual pricing-collusion replication.
reasons.C2: Real runs, pre-registration, contamination recall check, scripted baselines; but one model family, only 4 pools, and known-effect arms still pending.
reasons.C3: Eight-panel human-vs-agent figure and scorecard are clear; 9 pages over cap and 18 unresolved placeholders hurt.

levers.C1: Show a regime ranking that differs from humans robustly across two providers and state what an authority should change.
levers.C2: Run the known-effect arms, add a second provider, and expand beyond 4 pools so bootstrap intervals are meaningful.
levers.C3: Fill every placeholder, cut to 8 pages, and lead with the one finding that differs most from humans.

V3.verdict: Most on-target collusion experiment here with a real human benchmark and good hygiene; needs the pending arms and more pools to be convincing.

reasons.C1: Secret price-fixing offers to pricing agents is a sensible, moderately novel question with a clean say-versus-do split.
reasons.C2: Careful preregistration and many tests, but zero real model runs, no model chosen, no results.
reasons.C3: No report or demo seen; only a README dual-use note and design material.

levers.C1: Show that sellers act on offers they verbally reject, or vice versa, across two model families.
levers.C2: Execute the 60 preregistered games on real models and report acceptance and price outcomes with Wilson intervals.
levers.C3: Write the report with one figure contrasting stated acceptance and actual pricing per condition, plus limitations appendix.

D2.verdict: Well-designed harness and frozen preregistration, but without a single real run there is nothing to evaluate yet.

reasons.C1: Real agent-payment ledgers are an interesting setting, but wallets are not shown to be LLM agents and self-funding detection resembles known wash-trading heuristics.
reasons.C2: Held-out split, permutation test, synthetic positive control; but labels share the rule's evidence, and on independent features accuracy drops to 0.67, p = 0.14.
reasons.C3: 17 pages far exceeds the cap; the circularity caveat and main claim compete for attention.

levers.C1: Demonstrate the flagged wallets are LLM agents and show the method catches collusion that a standard wash-trading detector misses.
levers.C2: Obtain labels independent of transfer-graph evidence and show significant held-out accuracy on more than 10 families.
levers.C3: Cut to 8 pages and lead with the independent-feature result alongside the headline number.

C9.verdict: Honest observational work on real ledgers, but circular labels and unproven agent identity leave the main result shaky.

reasons.C1: Rival coalitions against each other is a neglected framing beyond single-coalition-versus-principal studies; Opus refusing blocs is an interesting finding.
reasons.C2: 144 real episodes, preregistration with hashes, no-rival arm; but no positive control, post-freeze measure change, key effect p = 0.055.
reasons.C3: No report seen; findings are a list of disparate metrics without one stated conclusion or limitations appendix.

levers.C1: Show rivalry robustly changes within-coalition cohesion on uninstructed agents across models, with a clear safety implication.
levers.C2: Add a positive control with known bloc formation, rerun the corrected defection measure on fresh seeds, and power the key comparison.
levers.C3: Deliver an 8-page report with one headline claim, one cell figure, and the limitations and dual-use appendix.

G6.verdict: Fresh question with real runs and good preregistration discipline, but missing positive control and report make claims hard to trust.
